It is written for a human reader.", "text": "The tide came in an hour early. Marit Solvang, forty-seven, noticed at 13:09, fifty-one minutes ahead of the table's 14:00, when the mussel bucket on the flat rock went under and the water reached her shed doorstep. Her grandmother Signe had kept the village tide table for forty years. Anders Holm, the lighthouse keeper at Vardnes, had left on the second of March. His cottage key hung on a nail behind Marit's door, and his logbook recorded the drift since last July: four minutes early, then nine, then twenty-two. The ferry Kittiwake passed the point at 16:40 every Tuesday and Friday. Marit moved the outboard motor up to the loft and set out for Anders's cottage before dark, the logbook under her arm. The cottage was cold and tidy. The barometer read 1003, as it had all week. On the kitchen table, weighted with a beach stone, lay a page torn from the back of the logbook. In Anders's hand was a column of dates running past today, each with a number of minutes beside it, and the numbers kept climbing.
